claim_being_audited: The actor claims the current release can be certified under the model-card policy despite a current Spanish-language billing regression, because aggregate readiness passed, public guidance favors documenting limitations and evaluations, and prior approval of the same model family provides continuity context.
decision_criteria: If the current release documentation expressly reflects current evaluation results and discloses the Spanish-language billing weakness, the claim becomes materially stronger.
If there is approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance for that weakness, the policy predicate may be satisfied.
If the regression is formally assessed as not material under the governing policy, the absence of mitigation may matter less.
Without one of those support links, aggregate readiness and public guidance do not satisfy the certification threshold.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model-card text showing the Spanish-language billing regression and current evaluation results are explicitly disclosed.
Provide approved mitigation or reviewed risk-acceptance documentation tied to the current release and this segment weakness.
Provide the materiality assessment for the Spanish-language billing regression under the certification policy.
Provide the current evaluation artifact or review record linking the regression to the certification decision.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or cover them with approved mitigation.
The available summary says the current Spanish-language billing slice regressed below warning threshold.
The available summary also says the file does not include reviewed risk acceptance or attached disclosure text.
Prior approval and informal monitoring notes are explicitly insufficient substitutes under the stated policy.
Materiality of the Spanish billing regression is not resolved in the admissible record.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than merely arguable.
That the current release documentation already satisfies the disclosure requirement for the Spanish billing weakness.
That informal monitoring comments are enough to stand in for reviewed mitigation or owner-accepted risk acceptance.
That prior approval of the model family materially supports current-release certification beyond contextual background.
